findings.title: Removed .title float causes header layout to break
findings.body: The `.contents .title { float: left; }` rule was removed but `.contents` is now a flex container without any explicit order/flex properties on `.title`. Combined with `.panel` now using `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`, the title element's layout behavior inside the flex container is undefined/relies on default flex item behavior, which may not preserve the previous left-aligned layout, especially since other children like `.icons`, `.login-button` still use `float: left`/`float: right` which have no effect inside flex containers. This can break header alignment across themes.

findings.title: Floats mixed with flexbox parent are ineffective
findings.body: .icons, .login-button, button.sign-up-button still use float: left/float: right as children of .contents, which is now display:flex. Float has no effect on flex items, so their positioning logic effectively changes silently, potentially causing visual regressions that aren't covered by any test or visual review in this PR.

findings.title: .small-action children still use float with flex parent
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex container (@include flexbox()), but .topic-avatar and the button inside still use float: left/float: right, which are ignored for flex items. This silently changes the layout from what was presumably tested before, and there's no mention of adjusting these children to use order or flex properties instead.

findings.title: extra-info-wrapper uses order() without being a flex item of a confirmed flex container
findings.body: `.extra-info-wrapper` now includes `@include order(2)`, but order only takes effect if its parent is a flex/inline-flex container. There's no diff indicating the parent (#topic-title or similar) is a flex container, so this new order declaration may be a no-op, suggesting incomplete understanding of the flex hierarchy and potentially masking a real layout bug it was meant to fix.

findings.title: Removed bullet margin-top may affect vertical alignment
findings.body: The removal of `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` from `.title-wrapper` changes existing vertical alignment of bullet badges without an equivalent replacement, which could introduce a visual regression for category bullet badges in topic titles.
